title: Fixed vs variable costs: CapEx and OpEx

kcs.statement: Fixed costs, such as buying servers and data center space up front, are paid whether or not the capacity is used; this up-front spending is capital expenditure (CapEx).
Variable costs rise and fall with actual usage; in the cloud, spending becomes operational expenditure (OpEx) for only the resources consumed.
With fixed on-premises capacity, an organisation must size for forecast peak demand, so capacity sits idle most of the time or runs out when demand beats the forecast.

problem_ideas: A company buys 10 servers at $6,000 each for a peak it reaches 1 month a year: compute the yearly idle capacity in server-months.
Classify six line items (server purchase, hourly instance fee, building lease, per-GB storage) as fixed or variable.
Predict the monthly bill when usage drops 60% under pay-as-you-go versus owned hardware.
A CFO wants to avoid a $500,000 up-front purchase: which cloud benefit answers this?
Forecast was 1,000 users and 5,000 arrived: describe what happens on premises versus in the cloud.
Spot the wrong statement: 'Moving to AWS turns OpEx into CapEx.'
